question_text: A city ordinance prohibits discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity (SOGI) in employment, housing, and public services. A business owner refuses to serve a customer because of the customer's SOGI, claiming freedom of religion. Which of the following best describes the legal situation?

options.text: The business owner's freedom of religion prevails over the anti-discrimination ordinance.
The anti-discrimination ordinance is unconstitutional because it infringes on religious freedom.
The anti-discrimination ordinance is a valid exercise of police power, and the business owner must comply.
The ordinance applies only to government services, not private businesses.
